A future congressman, Edward Everett, wrote to the Speaker of the House, Robert C. Winthrop, asking for “plenty of well sounding Indian words” to name the territory “rather than recognize this wretched imposture” of Deseret (Edward Everett letter to Robert C. Winthrop, Dec. 1, 1849, Edward Everett Letters, Za Letter File, Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, Yale University; Robert C. Winthrop letter to Edward Everett, Dec. 11, 1849, Edward Everett Papers, 1675–1910, Microfilm Edition, Massachusetts Historical Society). At first, congressmen usedUtahandDeseretinterchangeably, but within a couple of months, they silently dropped use of the termDeseret(The Congressional Globe,31st Congress, 1st session, 94, 99–100, 166–68, 211–13; 32nd Congress, 1st session, 1413–16).
See Grow and others, eds.,Council of Fifty, Minutes, March 1844–January 1846,521–22.
